title: Beating Others to Thank You
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece offers a specific relationship-building tactic for leaders: proactively thanking someone for a favor or effort before they have the chance to thank you for yours. It starts from the well-established idea that thankfulness draws people closer, then adds a twist — that thanking someone for something they were about to thank you for is a more powerful and disarming move than simply waiting to receive gratitude. Using the example of covering a presentation for a colleague, the article shows how flipping the sequence of gratitude changes the emotional dynamic of the exchange. The piece insists sincerity is a precondition, but frames the tactic as a learnable habit that deepens relationships when practiced consistently.
points: The essay's distinct contribution is a sequencing insight: thanking someone before they thank you is more relationally powerful than simply being thankful in general.
It uses a specific, relatable scenario (covering a presentation for a colleague) to make the abstract tactic concrete and repeatable.
It explicitly guards against the tactic becoming manipulative by insisting sincerity is a non-negotiable precondition.
It frames the practice as a discoverable habit — something a reader can start noticing opportunities for immediately, not a one-time gesture.
quotes: Frequently offering thanks makes others feel valued and respected. As an added bonus, the positive energy thankful people exude is both uplifting and contagious.
They have learned there is a strength in thanking others before they themselves get the chance to be thanked.
Instead of waiting for those thanks, those most skillful at relationships understand the connective power of beating them to the punch.
Thanking people for very things they would likely thank us for changes the script. It catches people off guard and shows them what a truly thankful person you are.
Make it a habit to thank people for what they are likely going to thank you for and beat them to it.
